400	So most people study the physical nefesh, but the physical nefesh belongs to the physical body, so truly it is not
401	the nefesh.
402	And also, this is not the essence of the nefesh behamit; it has many levels.
403	The sign, or the smallest branch of the nefesh behamit, is what we know in this world, which is
404	in the physical body, in the external desires, or in physical biochemistry, if you will.
405	But this is the lowest layer of the nefesh behamit.
406	The nefesh behamit expresses the private desire, the craving.
407	It is similar to vessels of the senses, which are the forces of desire within a person.
408	Now, there is the desire that comes from the side of the systems that rose to Binah, and there is the desire from the side of the separate systems.
409	And the distinction between them is really the distinction between the nefesh behamit of a Jew and of a gentile,
410	and we will learn about this later; the Tanya will also speak about it.
411	So it says that every element
412	in the nefesh behamit, which is also made up of ten sefirot, represents
413	the levels, the ladder of levels of the desires within it.
414	So it says there is anger and, by the way, pride, which comes from the element
415	of fire, which rises upward, so it is also on the highest level, and there is
416	the pleasures, which are physical pleasures or physical-soul pleasures, which come from the element
417	of water, and there is also the matter of
418	boasting, of vain things, lashon hara, which is the element of wind.
419	And there is laziness and depression and the desire for
420	excessive rest, which comes from the element of earth.
421	These are forces that exist in a person, not only physically; it's a sign, but there can be a person who has sports,
422	who is an expert marathon runner,
423	in the physical sense.
424	But if he comes to run for the service of HaShem, suddenly he is the heaviest old man in the world.
425	And we see disabled tzaddikim who are the fastest in the world spiritually.
426	So we are not talking about the physical; it is only a sign.
427	Still, the Rambam says it is important that the physical body be good, that we not be disturbed by it, so that we can serve HaShem.
428	Yes, everything is good: eat healthy, take care, exercise.
429	But the gentiles also do the work on character traits.
430	Therefore, I will speak about this later: for us, we have no interest in correcting the nefesh behamit for the sake of
431	its character traits, but we do it in order to reveal the nefesh elokit; it
432	is not for its own sake.
433	Therefore it says,
434	"And also the good traits in the nature of all Israel from their birth, such as compassion and gemach, come from it."
435	Kindnesses, because in Israel the nefesh is from the klipah, it is klipat Nogah, which also has good in it,
436	it is from the element of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil.
437	That is, naturally, when a person does not keep the mitzvot for their own sake, it is like the good of
438	conscience, or external good.
439	Why is it that this one has it and others do not?
